newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Juppe set to resign, to see Chirac.
newsitem.headline: France's Juppe set to resign, to see Chirac.

text.p: France's outgoing Prime Minister Alain Juppe will meet President Jacques Chirac at 9 a.m. (0700 GMT) on Monday and is set to resign after a stinging election defeat for his centre-right government, Chirac's office said.
Juppe said last week he would resign on Monday irrespective of the outcome of Sunday's runoff ballot in which the Socialist-led opposition won a majority in the National Assembly.

Chirac has to receive Juppe's formal resignation and the final results of the parliamentary election, likely later on Monday morning, before naming Socialist opposition leader Lionel Jospin as prime minister, probably later in the day.
Jospin could then start work on forming a cabinet to rule in a hostile tandem with conservative Chirac.

The Socialist-led opposition captured a majority in the 577-seat National Assembly in which the centre-right had controlled 80 percent of the seats. Juppe said he would resign after the left won more votes than the right on the first round of voting a week ago.
Chirac had called the vote 10 months early, wrongly thinking that voters would re-elect his centre-right allies in support of a single European currency from a position of strength.
